media_src: D, Oct. 14, 2026: the daltoncorr.com page's 13 posters in its order and pairs, each with its year and its period research under it, from D's Red Mask Production Art Tracker (April 2025): the year, the five films studied and the era's look, with what the poster shows.

media.label: Red Mask: Night of Blood, 1982
note: Painted, not photographed: a hooded figure in deep shadow, a screaming girl and a heavy slab title, the dark, illustrated one-sheet of the early ’80s.
References: “Poltergeist,” “The Thing,” “Creepshow,” “Basket Case” and “Friday the 13th Part III.”

media.label: Red Mask Part 2, 1984
note: One color, a torn edge and a dripping title, the mask looming over a girl in bed: by 1984 a single bold image told the story.
References: “A Nightmare on Elm Street,” “Children of the Corn,” “Gremlins,” “Silent Night, Deadly Night” and “Firestarter.”

media.label: Red Mask 3D: Crimson Wave, 1986
note: Red and cyan type that seems to want 3-D glasses, as third entries went 3-D (“Friday the 13th Part III,” “Jaws 3-D”). Surreal and lurid, as mid-’80s horror grew gorier and more colorful.
References: “Aliens,” “The Fly,” “Night of the Creeps,” “Poltergeist II” and “Critters.”

media.label: Red Mask 4: Trail of Terror, 1988
note: The villain is the poster: half scream, half mask in one painted panel on a deep blue field, the iconic, dark but colorful look of the late ’80s.
References: “Child’s Play,” “Pumpkinhead,” “Hellbound: Hellraiser II,” “Night of the Demons” and “Waxwork.”

media.label: Red Mask 5: A New Frontier, 1989
note: A photographed heroine under a giant cracked mask, a chrome title and a summer opening date: vivid color and dramatic light, the studio sequel of 1989.
References: “Pet Sematary,” “Puppet Master,” “Shocker,” “Society” and “Intruder.”

media.label: Red Mask VI: Knock Knock, 1991
note: Paint gives way to photographic realism: a lone door in a beam of light, a quieter, psychological threat, and the numbering turns Roman.
References: “The Silence of the Lambs,” “Child’s Play 3,” “The People Under the Stairs,” “Popcorn” and “Freddy’s Dead.”

media.label: Red Mask VII: Karina’s Revenge, 1993
note: Almost all black: one sliver of light, the mask and a face in the gap. Early-’90s posters stripped down to one stark image.
References: “Leprechaun,” “Cronos,” “Jason Goes to Hell,” “Needful Things” and “Body Snatchers.”

media.alt: Red Mask VIII: Alone in the Dark, 1995.
media.label: Red Mask VIII: Alone in the Dark, 1995
note: Low light, one porch lamp and a carved serif title: darker and moodier, the mid-’90s let texture and restraint carry the dread.
References: “Se7en,” “Village of the Damned,” “Candyman: Farewell to the Flesh,” “Species” and “Tales from the Crypt: Demon Knight.”

media.alt: Red Mask IX: The Death Knell, 1999.
media.label: Red Mask IX: The Death Knell, 1999
note: Spare and nearly dark, every earlier film counting down to IX, and a web address in the fine print, the year “The Blair Witch Project” sold itself online.
References: “The Blair Witch Project,” “The Sixth Sense,” “Sleepy Hollow,” “Audition” and “House on Haunted Hill.”

media.alt: Red Mask X: Beyond the Mask, 2001.
media.label: Red Mask X: Beyond the Mask, 2001
note: Photoreal and cold blue, the mask behind crossed knives, with an AOL Keyword under the title, as studio posters carried them at the turn of the century.
References: “Jeepers Creepers,” “The Others,” “Thirteen Ghosts,” “Session 9” and “Hannibal.”

media.label: Red Mask XI: Magnum Opus, 2003
note: One visceral close-up, a scream painted in blood, and the star’s name spaced across the top: graphic and intense, like the horror of 2003.
References: “Freddy vs. Jason,” “House of 1000 Corpses,” “Wrong Turn,” “Darkness Falls” and “High Tension.”

media.label: Red Mask XII: The Fight, 2005
note: Red and black on a diagonal, a hatchet raised behind her: blunt, gritty and brutal, the year of “Hostel,” “Saw II” and “Wolf Creek.”
References: “The Descent,” “Hostel,” “Wolf Creek,” “Saw II” and “The Devil’s Rejects.”

media.label: Red Mask 13: Unlucky Strike, 2007
note: One object and a neon title, a slot machine stopped on 13: late-2000s posters turned minimal as supernatural horror came back.
References: “Paranormal Activity,” “Trick ’r Treat,” “30 Days of Night,” “The Mist” and “REC.”
